jobs.title: Social Media Senior Manager
jobs.description:
Your wellbeing, our mission. Join a company shaping a healthier world.

GET TO KNOW US

At Wellhub we're revolutionizing workplace wellness. Our platform connects employees worldwide to the best partners for fitness, mindfulness, therapy, nutrition, and sleep—all in one simple subscription. Headquartered in NYC with team members in Europe, North America and South America, we're on a mission to make every company a wellness company.

We believe work should be fulfilling, inspiring, and balanced. Here, you'll find a team that values wellbeing, collaboration, and different perspectives, where passion and creativity push boundaries to create real impact. Your contributions will help shape a healthier, more balanced world for you and millions of people globally. 

Join us in redefining the future of wellbeing!

 

THE OPPORTUNITY

We're looking for a Senior Manager of Social Media who will own the shaping and execution of our UK social media strategy and lead social media managers across all European markets where Wellhub operates. As the most senior Social Media professional in Europe, you'll be the regional lead for the team and the primary social media partner for senior stakeholders.In this role, you'll partner closely with our Senior Director of Global Social Media to bring the UK strategy to life—creating platform-specific content, developing cultural relevance, supporting local influencer and ambassador programs, and elevating Wellhub's presence across key platforms like Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, YouTube, and emerging channels.You're someone who lives and breathes social. You understand UK culture deeply. You know how to move fast, test fearlessly, and capture moments in real time. You have a video-first mindset and love being behind—and occasionally in front of—the camera.You'll combine hands-on UK ownership with European team management, stakeholder leadership, and accountability for regional alignment and performance. Your creativity, agility, and understanding of UK social trends will shape how consumers, partners, and companies experience Wellhub.

YOUR IMPACT

  • Shape and Execute the UK Social Media Strategy.
  • Shape, localize, and operationalize Wellhub's social media strategy for the UK market.
  • Build regionally relevant content plans tailored for B2C, B2B, and B2P audiences.
  • Support Wellhub's GEO efforts through content strategy, partnering with relevant teams and European social media managers to align content priorities and strengthen brand authority and discoverability across the region.
  • Manage the editorial calendar for the UK and ensure seamless alignment with global priorities, launches, campaigns, and cultural moments.
  • Lead Social Media Managers Across Europe.
  • Manage, coach, and develop social media managers across all European markets where Wellhub operates, setting clear objectives, supporting professional growth, and enabling local ownership.
  • Set regional priorities with the Senior Director of Global Social Media, align local plans with global strategy, and establish regular planning and performance reviews.
  • Share insights and successful formats across countries, resolve competing priorities, and represent the European social team in global discussions.
  • Create High Impact Video First Content Concept, script, shoot, and edit content optimized for Reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts, and LinkedIn.
  • Capture spontaneous, social-worthy moments at local events, content shoots, and partner activations.
  • Work with creative and production colleagues to bring fresh ideas to life.
  • Drive Cultural Relevance.
  • Identify UK cultural trends, memes, humor, and moments that Wellhub can authentically participate in.Adapt global narratives to fit the UK social landscape and audience expectations.
  • Monitor competitor activity and industry trends to keep Wellhub culturally and creatively ahead.
  • Lead Local Ambassador and Influencer Execution.
  • Support the development and execution of influencer and ambassador programs in the UK
  • Partner with creators and wellness influencers who authentically represent the Wellhub brand.
  • Manage briefings, content feedback, deliverables, and performance tracking.
  • Lead Stakeholder Relationships Across Europe
  • Act as the most senior Social Media representative in Europe and the primary partner for regional leadership, country leaders, and senior marketing, sales, people, PR, and partner stakeholders.
  • Build alignment on social strategy, priorities, and expectations across European markets.
  • Guide decisions, constructively challenge requests, and resolve escalations while protecting local relevance and global brand consistency.
  • Collaborate with UK marketing, sales, people, PR, and partner teams to amplify locally relevant moments.Work closely with the global creative team to align content quality, storytelling, sonic identity, and brand voice.
  • Support country leaders and internal spokespeople with social content, thought leadership, and engagement guidance. 
  • Own Measurement Optimisation and Insights.
  • Track and report on performance metrics across awareness, engagement, growth, and sentiment.Test new formats, creative variations, and posting strategies to continuously improve results.
  • Conduct social listening to understand audience behavior and guide content direction.
  • Review performance across European markets with local social managers and turn shared learnings into regional recommendations and improvements.
  • Community Engagement and Brand Advocacy
  • Oversee proactive community management across the UK channels—engaging in conversations, responding to comments, and cultivating brand advocates.
  • Ensure alignment with global crisis and response protocols.

WHO YOU ARE

  • You have 7+ years of experience in social media, content creation, or digital marketing—ideally in fast-moving B2C or lifestyle brands.
  • You're fluent in UK social culture, humor, trends, and how different audiences behave online.
  • You have excellent English writing and editorial skills.
  • You're a video-first creator who is comfortable planning, shooting, editing—and occasionally stepping in front of the camera.
  • You're obsessed with social platforms: their algorithms, nuances, and emerging formats.
  • You understand how to speak to diverse audiences—consumers, HR leaders, corporate buyers, wellness partners.
  • You're highly creative, but also organized and able to manage calendars, workflows, approvals, and reporting.
  • You have experience managing and developing social media teams across markets, with the judgement and autonomy to serve as the senior regional lead.
  • You can influence senior stakeholders, explain your recommendations, manage difficult conversations, and align regional priorities with local needs.
  • You excel in ambiguous, fast-paced environments and aren't afraid to test new ideas.
  • You're a collaborative team player who values feedback, teamwork, and cross-functional partnership.
  • You're proactive, curious, and passionate about wellbeing and digital storytelling.

We recognize that individuals approach job applications differently. We strongly encourage all aspiring applicants to go for it, even if they don't match the job description 100%. We welcome your application and will be delighted to explore if you could be a great fit for our team. 

WHAT WE OFFER YOU

With thoughtful benefits, emotional wellbeing resources, and a culture that empowers you to take ownership of your role and your wellbeing, we create an environment where you can thrive in all dimensions of your life. Our benefits include:

WELLHUB:  Free Gold membership with access to onsite gyms and studios, digital fitness programs, and online wellness resources for meditation, nutrition, mental wellbeing support, and more! Add up to three family members to your plan, ensuring access to wellness for those who matter most to you.

HEALTHCARE: Health and dental insurance. 

FLEXIBLE SCHEDULE:  Flexibility for us isn't just about where we work—it also means being able to shape how and when we get things done. Together with their leaders, employees define schedules that align with their time zones, team needs, and personal routines.

PAID TIME OFF: We know how important it is to take time away from work to recharge. Employees receive a minimum of 25 days paid holiday per year with an additional day for each year of tenure (up to 5) in addition to annual holidays (including an extra holiday on your birthday!). 

PARENTAL LEAVE: Welcoming a new child is one of the most special moments in your life. Take the time to be present and enjoy your growing family. We offer 100% paid parental leave to all new parents. Parents giving birth are eligible for an extended leave and a ramp-back period to return part-time while they get settled.  

CAREER GROWTH: Access world-class platforms, participate in interactive sessions,  build your personalized development roadmap, and explore internal opportunities. We focus on continuous learning and feedback to support your journey toward personal and professional success. 

CULTURE: You'll join a team of passionate people who come together to break boundaries, support each other, and create a meaningful impact in workplace wellness. We win together, building trust through open communication and a culture where every perspective matters. Learn more about our shared culture and values here. 

 

Want to see what it's really like to work here? Follow us on Instagram @lifeatwellhub and watch our team video on YouTube!

Diversity, Equity, and Belonging at Wellhub

We aim to create a collaborative, supportive, and inclusive space where everyone knows they belong. 

Wellhub is committed to creating a diverse work environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, non-disqualifying physical or mental disability, national origin, veteran status, or any other basis covered by appropriate law.

Our commitment to inclusion also extends to how we recognize and reward our people. We're proud to be Syndio Fair Pay Certified, reflecting our ongoing dedication to equitable and fair pay practices across our global team. Read more about it here.

Questions on how we treat your personal data? See our Job Applicant Privacy Notice.

jobs.title: Senior CRM Executive - Lifecycle
jobs.description:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

About the team

This position will be part of the central CRM & Ops team, composed of 18+ specialists, dedicated to driving and executing global strategic initiatives to grow and retain our New Customer base. Collectively, the team is targeted on growing orders, expanding our subscriber base, improving engagement metrics to retain Deliveroo customers. Serving as the voice of the customer, the CRM & Ops team does this by enhancing personalised user experiences, activating best-in-class campaigns, and putting relevancy at the heart of everything. 

The Role

As a Marketing Manager within the Lifecycle CRM & Ops team you are the voice of Deliveroo when speaking with our customers across the globe. You'll operate under a hybrid work model, spending a minimum of three days a week at our London HQ.

Reporting into the Senior Marketing Manager on the New Customer squad, and working closely with stakeholders across Product, Engineering, Global CRM, Marketing Promotions, and Data Science, You'll be a technical, commercially minded CRM marketer who is hands-on in the tooling: building Lifecycle journeys, setting up experiments and audiences, and configuring promotions and in-app merchandising. You'll have end-to-end ownership of the New Customer Lifecycle, from journey design and build through to measurement and ROI. You'll also use personalisation and AI to make journeys more relevant. Your primary focus will be on creating customer-centric journeys that are highly relevant, using the right channels at the right time to deliver meaningful business impact, while working with local markets as you scale your initiatives internationally. 

What you'll be doing

  • Collaborate with multiple stakeholders to support growing the new customer base by combining data-driven insights with CRM best practice to initiate and deliver programs internationally 
  • Build and configure multi-channel journeys (email, push, in-app), including audience logic, triggers, testing and QA
  • Design and build multi-variant Lifecycle experiments
  • Create promotions for new customer acquisition and retention, ensuring accurate setup, targeting and tracking
  • Manage in-app merchandising placements, working with Product and Marketing Promotions
  • Deliver personalisation at scale, and test where AI can improve content and efficiency
  • Own operational delivery, optimisation, reporting of campaigns and weekly trading
  • Proactively monitor and report on campaigns to stakeholders & propose/manage changes and optimisations where necessary
  • Collaborate with the New Customer Lifecycle Manager and Marketing Promotions teams to develop the global CRM new customers lifecycle strategy
  • Collaborate with stakeholders on key projects to create and implement test strategies that optimises performance of new & existing campaigns
  • Be comfortable with data targeting, segmentation & analysis - pulling it, manipulating it and interpreting it, whilst using marketing technology to help achieve customer touchpoints faster and more efficiently than ever before
  • Drive innovative ideas and solutions in response to business and customer needs
  • Provide regular communication with stakeholders, such as the central marketing team, product and engineering teams and local markets, to ensure workloads & deadlines are managed efficiently (we love Slack channels for everything)
  • Conduct post campaign reporting, pulling out the most interesting lessons and using these to guide your future ideas

Requirements

  • Bachelor's Degree (Marketing or Business preferred) or strong relevant experience
  • A minimum of 3+ years CRM experience
  • Can work in a fast-paced environment and prioritise workload
  • Attention to detail and campaign deadlines are adhered to, maintaining high standards of accuracy
  • Highly computer literate with:
    • HTML familiarity (ability to understand where changes need to be made)
    • Liquid logic 
  • Technical knowledge in CRM automation development
  • Good communication skills and ability to coordinate with multiple stakeholders groups
  • Data visualisation tools & reporting experience (Looker preferred)

jobs.title: Barne- og ungdomsarbeider
jobs.description:
Vil du vere med og skape gode dagar for barn? Fagteamet i barnehagane i Klepp kommune søkjer fagarbeidarar med oppstart snarast mogleg. Fagteamet arbeider for at barn med behov for ekstra støtte skal få gode, trygge og utviklande dagar i barnehagen. Gjennom spesialpedagogiske tiltak og andre nødvendige støttetiltak følgjer vi opp mål som er fastsette i sakkunnige vurderingar og vedtak. Vi er opptekne av å sjå det enkelte barnet sine ressursar og moglegheiter, og arbeider kvar dag for å skape gode opplevingar, meistring og tilhøyrsle i fellesskapet. Som tilsett i fagteamet får du vere med på eit viktig arbeid som kan gjere ein stor forskjell i barn sine liv.Vi ser etter deg som har eit stort hjarte for barn og som ønskjer å bidra til at barn får oppleve tryggleik, meistring og utvikling i kvardagen. Hos oss får du arbeide tett på barna i kommunale og private barnehagar i Klepp kommune. Vi er opptekne av nærvær, relasjonar og tidleg innsats, og vi ønskjer medarbeidarar som trivst i direkte arbeid med barn. Som fagarbeidar i fagteamet vil du vere ein viktig støttespelar for barn som treng litt ekstra oppfølging for å få best mogleg utvikling og deltaking i barnehagekvardagen. 

Arbeidsoppgåver
  • Direkte arbeid med barn individuelt og i grupper 
  • Bidra til å skape trygge, gode og inkluderande miljø for barn 
  • Delta i gjennomføring av tiltak kring barn med særskilde behov 
  • Støtte barna i leik, læring og sosial utvikling 
  • Samarbeide tett med føresette og tilsette i barnehagane, og med tilsette og leiarteamet i Fagteamet.  
  • Bidra til at barna opplever meistring og fellesskap i kvardagen 
Kvalifikasjonar
  • Fagbrev som barne- og ungdomsarbeidar 
  • Vidareutdanning innan spesialpedagogikk er ønskjeleg 
  • Anna relevant vidareutdanning eller erfaring frå arbeid med barn vil bli vektlagt 
  • Erfaring frå arbeid med barn med særskilde behov er ein fordel 
  • Gode ferdigheiter i norsk, både munnleg og skriftleg.
  • Den som får tilbod om stillinga, må leggje fram politiattest, jf. barnehagelova § 19. Attesten skal ikkje vere eldre enn tre månader.
  • Førarkort klasse B 
  • Personleg eignaheit vil bli vektlagt.
Personlege eigenskapar
  • Vi ønskjer oss ein kollega som 
  • Møter barn med varme, omsorg og respekt 
  • Er til stades og byggjer trygge relasjonar 
  • Ser moglegheiter og ressursar hos kvart enkelt barn 
  • Samarbeider godt med både føresette og kollegaer 
  • Er positiv, engasjert og fleksibel 
  • Ønskjer å bidra til eit godt arbeidsmiljø og eit sterkt fagleg fellesskap 
  • Har ei helse som er foreneleg med det å arbeida i barnehage.  
Vi tilbyr
  • Hos oss får du 
  • Eit viktig og meiningsfylt arbeid med barn 
  • Moglegheit til å gjere ein forskjell kvar dag 
  • Eit varmt, inkluderande og støttande arbeidsmiljø 
  • Samarbeid med dyktige og engasjerte kollegaer 
  • Varierte arbeidsdagar med høg grad av nærvær i arbeidet med barna 
  • Gode pensjons- og forsikringsordningar gjennom Klepp kommune 
  • Tett oppfølgjing frå leiarteamet i Fagteamet.  
KontaktinformasjonTrine Vika Tengesdal, Styrar, +47 93021953 ArbeidsstadEngrappstubben 1 4351 Kleppe Nøkkelinformasjon:Arbeidsgivar: Klepp kommune Referansenr.: 5209106548 Stillingsprosent: 100% Fast Søknadsfrist: 29.11.2026

Om arbeidsgiveren:

Klepp er den største av kommunane på Jæren, med over 21 000 innbyggarar og om lag 1800  tilsette. Me ligg sentralt til, med korte avstander både til Stavanger, Sandnes og Bryne.

Kommunen vår har dei flottaste strendene i heile regionen, me har ein spennande kulturhistorie, og ei god blanding av landbruk, industri og varehandel.

Visjonen vår er «Med blikk for alle».  Me ønskjer tilsette som tek i eit tak, bryr seg og tenkjer fritt, og me oppmodar alle kvalifiserte til å søkja, uansett alder, kjønn, funksjonsevne, seksuell orientering, religion eller etnisk bakgrunn.

Me gjer merksam på at søkarlister kan verta offentleggjort, sjølv om ein har bede om å bli unntatt offentlegheit. Søkar vil verta varsla før offentleggjering.

jobs.title: (Senior) Implementation Consultant (m/w/d)
jobs.description:
Die Baubranche ist eine 14-Billionen-Euro-Industrie, die noch immer auf E-Mails, Excel-Tabellen und eingescannten PDFs läuft. Cosuno ersetzt das durch KI. Generalunternehmer schreiben ihre Projekte auf unserer Plattform an mehr als 250.000 Nachunternehmer aus, und unsere agentische KI findet die passenden Firmen, erkennt Auffälligkeiten in Angeboten und vergleicht jeden Preis mit 6,5 Millionen Datenpunkten aus über 136 Milliarden Euro verarbeitetem Angebotsvolumen. 2019 in Berlin gegründet und von Cherry Ventures und Spark Capital mit über 40 Millionen Euro finanziert, skalieren wir jetzt Sales, Customer Success und Marketing. Dafür bauen wir ein eigenes Consulting-Team auf, und genau hier kommst du ins Spiel.


Die Rolle

Du übernimmst neue Kunden direkt nach der Unterschrift und bringst sie in den ersten 90 Tagen in die produktive Nutzung. Du leitest den Kick-off, klärst mit dem Kunden, wer ausschreibt und mit welchem Projekt es losgeht, schulst Einkauf, Kalkulation und Projektleitung und sorgst dafür, dass die ersten Ausschreibungen rausgehen und Angebote zurückkommen. Wenn ein Kunde hängt, merkst du es früh und drehst ihn, notfalls über die Geschäftsführung. Nach 90 Tagen übergibst du ihn mit klarem Stand an seinen Account Manager.

Du begleitest viele Kunden parallel, vom Familienbetrieb bis zum Generalunternehmer mit mehreren Niederlassungen. Als Senior Implementation Consultant übernimmst du die komplexen Einführungen: mehrere Standorte oder Gesellschaften, Freigabeprozesse, Systemlandschaften und viele Beteiligte. Und du entwickelst mit, wie unser Consulting-Team arbeitet.

Du berichtest an die Leiterin unseres Consulting-Teams.

Woran wir dich nach 12 Monaten messen

  • Deine Kunden sind nach 90 Tagen produktiv: Sie schreiben über Cosuno aus und erhalten Angebote, nachweisbar im Activation Report.

  • Jeder Kick-off endet mit klaren Zusagen: ausschreibende Nutzer, erstes Projekt, Termine, Mandat der Geschäftsführung.

  • Kunden, die hinter Plan liegen, haben schnell einen Plan, und die meisten holen auf.

  • Deine Kunden bewerten ihr Onboarding gut, und dein Account Manager weiß bei der Übergabe genau, wo der Kunde steht.

  • Als Senior: Deine komplexen Einführungen erreichen ihr Ziel, und das Team arbeitet mit Bausteinen, die du entwickelt hast.

Wer bei Cosuno erfolgreich ist

  • Ownership. Du sprichst über eigene Fehler, bevor jemand fragt, und darüber, was du daraus geändert hast.

  • Speed. Du löst Probleme pragmatisch und heute, nicht perfekt und nächstes Quartal.

  • Drive. Wenn ein Kunde hängt, rufst du an, statt auf die nächste Mail zu warten.

  • Low Ego. Du teilst, was bei dir funktioniert hat, damit das Team besser wird.

Diese Rolle ist für dich, wenn

  • du gern erklärst und es dich reizt, gerade die Skeptiker zu überzeugen.

  • du lieber vom Ziel rückwärts planst, als Schulungen abzuarbeiten.

  • du bei vielen Kunden parallel den Überblick behältst und weißt, wer heute deine Zeit bekommt.

  • du mit Kalkulatoren und Geschäftsführern gleichermaßen auf Augenhöhe sprichst.

  • du verstehen willst, wie am Bau eingekauft und vergeben wird.

Diese Rolle ist nichts für dich, wenn

  • du Onboarding als eine Reihe von Produktdemos verstehst.

  • du lieber in langen Projekten mit wenigen Kunden berätst als viele Kunden schnell zum Ergebnis zu bringen.

  • du wartest, bis der Kunde sich meldet.

Harte Anforderungen

jobs.title: Senior Staff Product Engineer
jobs.description:
About hyperexponential (hx)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry - which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

About the Engineering team

At hyperexponential, engineering is at the heart of our mission to transform the insurance industry. Our engineers build and scale, enabling insurers to model complex risks and make smarter pricing decisions at speed. By combining deep technical expertise with creativity, the team pushes the boundaries of what’s possible in insurance technology.

Within engineering, our product teams are cross-functional, pairing frontend and backend engineers with designers and product managers. This enables end-to-end ownership of features, with engineers contributing across design, architecture, implementation, and testing. Collaboration is a core part of how we work, ensuring that every release is both technically sound and valuable to our users.

How we work

We're in the middle of a deliberate shift in how hx builds. Everyone in product development is a Builder, and the Product Engineer is the default unit of how we work.

We organise around problems, not permanent teams. Small pods, usually of two to four Product Engineers, form around the highest-value problem, own it end-to-end from discovery through to running it in production, and re-form as priorities change. Pods sit inside value streams, each owning a customer outcome and led by a Stream Lead who decides which problems the stream takes on and holds the bar for what ships. Your growth sits elsewhere: a Career Mentor owns your development and progression, so you can move to where the most important problem is without your career following the org chart.

We hire Product Engineers into hx, not into a fixed team, domain, or layer of the stack. You'll start in the stream where your strengths and our highest-value problems meet, and move as the problems move.

Product Engineers are T-shaped: deep expertise in software engineering, plus enough product and design judgement to make routine calls yourself. An embedded PM or designer raises a pod's ceiling on the hardest problems, but is never a gate between you and the customer. This is also a deliberately AI-native role, and one of the areas where we're moving fastest.

A pod of three owns its problem whole, which means going wherever it leads: front end, back end, data, or infrastructure. You don't need to be full-stack by trade, but you do need to be comfortable working outside your strongest layer.

The Product Engineer role is the same at every level. What scales is the size of the problem you own, how expensive your decisions are to reverse, and how far your judgement travels beyond your pod. At Level 5, that looks like this.

 

What you'll be doing

  • Taking a customer problem from discovery to production inside a pod, getting close to customers yourself, framing the problem, and shipping in small increments guided by real customer signal rather than internal opinion.

  • Directing AI agents to draft implementation, tests, and migrations, then reviewing, integrating, and hardening that work. You'll write intent precisely enough to brief both a teammate and an agent, and own correctness and maintainability regardless of how the first draft was produced.

  • Designing and delivering robust production systems where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency matter, with the tests and observability that make complex behaviour safe to evolve.

  • Working across the codebase wherever the problem leads, including areas your pod doesn't steward, with stewards looped in proportionate to the risk rather than handing work off and waiting.

  • Moving between pods, problems, and streams as priorities change, ramping fast on unfamiliar domains and leaving what you built running well behind you.

  • Taking full accountability for outcomes rather than just your code changes: raising risks early, and deciding rather than escalating.

What you'll need to have done

  • Built and shipped production systems end-to-end, from design through rollout, monitoring, and iteration, in settings where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency mattered.

  • Designed testing and observability that made complex behaviour understandable, debuggable, and safe to evolve.

  • Worked effectively in a polyglot environment, choosing the right tool for the problem and picking up unfamiliar languages, domains, and codebases fast. Strong systems experience, for example in Rust, C/C++, or Python, is valued, and we'll upskill you where there are gaps.

  • Shipped work outside your strongest layer of the stack when the problem needed it, picking up the front end, the data layer, or the infrastructure rather than waiting for someone else to.

  • Used AI tools as a serious part of how you build, with the judgement to direct, review, and stand behind what they produce.

  • Carried product and design judgement into your engineering work, shaping the solution rather than only implementing a spec and making sensible calls under ambiguity.

  • Owned outcomes beyond your immediate task, taking decisions rather than escalating them.

At Level 5 we'll also look for

  • Set technical direction on a hard problem other engineers built on, and been judged on whether you made them faster and safer rather than on the size of your team.

  • Held a quality bar across other people's work without becoming the gate they wait on.

  • Led cross-cutting or decoupling work that teams adopted because it was the best path, not because it was mandated.

 

You’re unlikely to thrive here if

  • You prefer following detailed instructions rather than experimenting and finding your own approach.

  • You are uncomfortable working directly with non-technical stakeholders to understand their challenges.

  • You avoid tackling ambiguous or open-ended problems where the solution isn’t obvious.

If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you’ll do your best work. We’re building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

 

Compensation

At hx, we’re committed to salary transparency. You’ll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we’re working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we’re building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don’t always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that’s competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

Benefits

£5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.

25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total).

Company pension scheme via Penfold.

Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life.

Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno.

Private healthcare insurance through AXA.

Income protection and Life Insurance.

Cycle to Work Scheme.

 

Additional perks

Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.).

Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights.

Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry.

Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.

 

Interview process

  1. Initial chat with our Talent team

  2. Lead Hirer Interview

  3. Live AI Skills Assessment

  4. Values Interview with the CPTO

  5. Meet the CEO

 

Our commitment to Diversity

hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.

Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.

If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

 

Next steps

If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome.

For more information about applying and to view other opportunities, you can visit our careers page.

Please note that background checks will be conducted as part of the hiring process to ensure compliance with our governance policies. We handle all background checks sensitively and in full compliance with relevant regulations.   • Directing AI agents to draft implementation, tests, and migrations, then reviewing, integrating, and hardening that work. You'll write intent precisely enough to brief both a teammate and an agent, and own correctness and maintainability regardless of how the first draft was produced.

  • Designing and delivering robust production systems where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency matter, with the tests and observability that make complex behaviour safe to evolve.

  • Working across the codebase wherever the problem leads, including areas your pod doesn't steward, with stewards looped in proportionate to the risk rather than handing work off and waiting.

  • Moving between pods, problems, and streams as priorities change, ramping fast on unfamiliar domains and leaving what you built running well behind you.

  • Taking full accountability for outcomes rather than just your code changes: raising risks early, and deciding rather than escalating.

What you'll need to have done

  • Built and shipped production systems end-to-end, from design through rollout, monitoring, and iteration, in settings where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency mattered.

  • Designed testing and observability that made complex behaviour understandable, debuggable, and safe to evolve.

  • Worked effectively in a polyglot environment, choosing the right tool for the problem and picking up unfamiliar languages, domains, and codebases fast. Strong systems experience, for example in Rust, C/C++, or Python, is valued, and we'll upskill you where there are gaps.

  • Shipped work outside your strongest layer of the stack when the problem needed it, picking up the front end, the data layer, or the infrastructure rather than waiting for someone else to.

  • Used AI tools as a serious part of how you build, with the judgement to direct, review, and stand behind what they produce.

  • Carried product and design judgement into your engineering work, shaping the solution rather than only implementing a spec and making sensible calls under ambiguity.

  • Owned outcomes beyond your immediate task, taking decisions rather than escalating them.

 

You’re unlikely to thrive here if

  • You prefer following detailed instructions rather than experimenting and finding your own approach.

  • You are uncomfortable working directly with non-technical stakeholders to understand their challenges.

  • You avoid tackling ambiguous or open-ended problems where the solution isn’t obvious.

If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you’ll do your best work. We’re building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

 

Compensation

At hx, we’re committed to salary transparency. You’ll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we’re working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we’re building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don’t always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that’s competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

Benefits

£5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.

25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total).

Company pension scheme via Penfold.

Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno.

Private healthcare insurance through AXA.

Cycle to Work Scheme.

 

Additional perks

Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.).

Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights.

Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry.

Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.

 

Interview process

  1. Initial chat with our Talent team

  2. Lead Hirer Interview

  3. Live AI Skills Assessment

  5. Meet the CEO

 

Our commitment to Diversity

hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.

Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.

jobs.description:
About Dust

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it.

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast.

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50.

The Role

We’re hiring a hands-on sales leader for the UK. You’ll build, lead, and coach the regional Sales team, deliver against ARR and pipeline goals, and build a repeatable local growth engine.

You'll act as the business lead for your market, with accountability for revenue. As a sales leader, you'll lead and coach the sales team, stay close to customers and deals, and build a repeatable sales approach that fits your market. As an orchestrator, you'll coordinate the local pipeline generation activities that feed your number, including marketing and pre-sales. You'll work closely with leaders across BDR, Growth, Field Marketing, Partnerships, Revenue Operations, Solutions Engineering, Deployment, and Customer Success, and influence how they support your market's priorities.

What you’ll do

  • Own the region’s ARR plan, forecast, and qualified pipeline. Work with the CRO to set priorities, understand capacity needs, and support the team to deliver against the plan.

  • Build and lead the regional Sales team. Hire, onboard, coach, and develop sellers, while staying hands-on in priority opportunities from prospecting and discovery through qualification, evaluation, negotiation, and close.

  • Make clear, evidence-based recommendations to Product based on regional customer conversations, deal patterns, and market needs. Build and refine a repeatable regional sales approach using pipeline, win/loss learning, and customer outcomes.

  • Drive the plan in partnership with field marketing to set priorities for events, campaigns, customer advocacy and community programs, and direct how field marketing resources are used to support your pipeline and ARR goals.

  • Partner with the marketing leadership, who own field marketing standards, methods and team management, to make sure regional programs are well executed, measured and consistent with Dust's broader marketing approach

  • Partner with BDR and Growth leaders to build a qualified pipeline through a deliberate mix of outbound and other locally effective channels.

  • Set direction for how Partnerships can support regional priorities. Work with the Partnerships lead to identify opportunities for sourcing, co-selling, or delivery.

  • Coordinate with Solutions Engineering, Deployment, Professional Services, and Customer Success to support credible evaluations, successful implementations, customer outcomes, and expansion.

  • Represent regional customer needs internally and share market learning with the CRO and functional leaders, contributing to consistent GTM practices across Dust.

Market-specific focus

United Kingdom

Build on early customer and partner traction. Use customer referrals, targeted events, and focused market experiments to build qualified pipeline and strengthen local customer proof.

What we’re looking for

  • A proven sales professional who has grown from individual contributor into people leadership, with 5+ years leading B2B software sales and coaching regional sales teams and a hands-on understanding of how to help reps succeed in-market.

  • You've owned a market or segment revenue number end to end, not just a team's quota. You've built pipeline through functions you didn't manage, such as marketing, partners and pre-sales, and you've made real calls about where capacity and budget go, including between direct sales and partners

  • Ability to lead by example in priority opportunities, from discovery through close.

  • Experience building pipeline and customer relationships in a market where the brand or sales motion is still developing.

  • A disciplined approach to forecasting and performance feedback, paired with high EQ and a genuinely supportive leadership style.

  • An appetite for building, testing, and refining a market over multiple quarters while balancing near-term results with durable growth.

What success looks like

The region delivers against its ARR and pipeline goals while developing a repeatable sales approach suited to local customers. The team builds customer trust and referenceable outcomes, cross-functional support is focused on regional priorities, and market learning informs Dust’s broader GTM approach.

Location

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.

Why this role exists

 

We are about to hire the people who will define the next phase of this company. Not backfill a plan someone else wrote — define it. The quality of who joins Dust over the next eighteen months is the single highest-leverage variable in whether we build the category or watch someone else do it.

 

That work needs a recruiter who treats hiring as a craft rather than a queue. Someone who can hold a real point of view on what "great" looks like for a role, defend it with a hiring manager who disagrees, and then go find that person themselves — from a cold start, without a lead gen team, a sourcing pod, or a playbook waiting for them.

 

You'll be an early member of a small Talent team. That means you own roles end to end, and you also help build the thing itself: the assessment design, the interview loops, the calibration, the data we use to know whether any of it is working.

 

We're looking for someone who cares about the candidate experience for all parties internal and external. And prioritizes protecting Dust's culture by being thoughtful, thorough and leading by example in being a true team player.

 
 

What you'll own

 

Full-cycle hiring, end to end. You run your own searches from role kickoff to close. Sourcing, outreach, screening, interviewing, offer strategy, negotiation. You are the owner of the outcome, not a coordinator of other people's opinions.

 

Assessment design, not just assessment delivery. For every role you open, you help define what evidence would actually predict success — then you build the loop that surfaces it. You'll push back on interview stages that exist out of habit and replace them with ones that test something real.

 

Hiring manager partnership with a spine. You'll spend as much time calibrating hiring managers as you do talking to candidates. When a manager says "not quite the right feel," you'll ask what they mean until there's a defensible answer, and you'll say so when there isn't one.

 

Market intelligence. You'll know your talent market better than anyone else in the building — who's good, where they are, what moves them, what compensation actually looks like right now — and you'll bring that back into how we scope roles and design offers.

 

The candidate experience. Our hiring process is the first honest sample of what working here feels like. You'll make it expedient, direct, well-communicated, and worth a candidate's time whether or not they get an offer.

 

Building the function. Process, tooling, structured scorecards, funnel data, quality-of-hire signal. You'll leave the system better than you found it, and you'll be trusted to change it without asking permission first.

 
 

Two tracks — tell us which one is yours

 

We're hiring for depth in one of two areas. You should have a genuine centre of gravity in one; interest in the other is a bonus, not a requirement.

 

GTM. Account Executives, Sales Engineers, Customer Success, Marketing, and the leaders above them, across Europe and the US. You know how to assess commercial talent on evidence rather than swagger, and you can tell the difference between a rep who carried a territory and a rep who inherited one.

 

Technical. Software engineers, infrastructure, product, and design, in a market where the best people are not looking and the second-best are drowning in outreach. You can hold a credible conversation about what someone actually built, and you know why that matters more than where they built it.

 
 

How we think about hiring

 

We're telling you this up front because if you disagree with it, this will be a frustrating job.

 

  • We don't hire based on pedigree. Logos and school names are weak evidence. What someone has actually done, and what they can demonstrate now, is strong evidence. We design our loops accordingly.

  • We hire for evidence, not affinity. "Culture fit" that means "reminds me of me" is how companies get homogeneous and slow. We assess against explicit behaviours tied to how we work, and we write down what we saw.

  • Speed and rigour are not in tension. Slow processes are usually a symptom of unclear thinking about the role, not of high standards.

  • A no should be as clear as a yes. To the candidate, and internally.

  • Some of us came from well-known companies. That's context, not criteria. It isn't why we're here and it won't be why you are. We celebrate everyone's achievements and want to create an environment where diversity of thought and experience of a collective whole makes this place exceptional and lasting.

  • Recruiters are operators, not order-takers. If you think a role is wrongly scoped, badly levelled, or shouldn't be open at all, you're expected to say so.

 
 

What we're looking for

 

  • 5+ years in full-cycle recruiting, with meaningful time in-house at a high-growth company. You've hired in an environment with real ambiguity, not just real volume.

  • Demonstrable depth in either GTM or technical hiring — you can talk through searches you've run, what made them hard, and what you'd do differently.

  • Genuinely strong sourcing. Not "I partner with a sourcing team." You find people yourself, and you write outreach that people reply to because it's obviously written by a human who read something.

  • Comfort operating without infrastructure. No playbook, no SDR equivalent, limited tooling to start.

  • The judgement and directness to challenge senior stakeholders, and the credibility to be listened to when you do.

  • A bias to start. You see the gap and close it before anyone asks you to.

  • Excellent written English and a real feel for language. Everything you write is a piece of our employer brand.

  • Low ego, high ownership. No job is too big or too small — you'll design an assessment framework in the morning and chase a scheduling conflict in the afternoon.

  • Based in Paris, London or New York.

 

Ideal, but not required: experience hiring in AI or developer-facing companies; experience building or improving a hiring process rather than inheriting one; multi-market hiring across Europe and the US.

 
 

You'll be using AI to do this job — properly

 

We build the AI operating system that companies use to rewire their work. We expect our own team to be the sharpest possible example of that.

 

You'll build and run your own Dust agents: market maps, candidate research, interview debrief synthesis, competitive intelligence on where talent is moving. Not as a side project — as how the job gets done. You don't need to have done this before, but you do need to be the kind of person who is genuinely excited to, rather than politely tolerant of it.

 

You'll also be one of our most credible internal sources of feedback on the product, because you'll be a heavy user of it every day.

 
 

Location

 

This role is based in Paris, London or New York, and we'd love you to spend real time in the office with the team. A lot of the best things about building at Dust happen because people are in the same room: the energy, the fast decisions, the unexpected conversation that unlocks a hard problem.

 

We hire people with strong judgement and extend that trust to how they manage their time.

 
 

Our process

 

We'll tell you the full loop up front, keep it to a small number of stages, and give you a decision quickly. You'll meet the people you'd work with, not a panel of proxies. Expect at least one stage where you work through a real hiring problem with us rather than describing a past one.

jobs.title: Marketing Operations
jobs.description:
Health can’t wait.

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

Marketing Ops is one of Alan's highest-leverage functions.

It sits at the intersection of marketing strategy, data, and technology — turning systems into growth engines and ensuring every touchpoint with prospects and members is timely, relevant, and scalable.

Alan is growing fast across France, Belgium, Spain, and Canada. But today we're leaving value on the table. On the prospect side, we drive more traffic but can't convert it properly: no scoring, no intelligent routing, no nurturing that adapts to buying intent. On the member side, messaging is one of our primary touchpoints for engagement, retention, and trust — yet nobody operates it strategically. Personalization stays shallow, communication pressure goes unmonitored, and shipping a message often means filing an engineering ticket.

We need Marketing Ops leaders who can architect scalable systems, operate them strategically, and progressively embed AI into workflows — to raise quality, reduce manual execution, and unlock growth without scaling headcount linearly.

⭐️ The Marketing Ops job ⭐️

We are hiring two Marketing Operations Managers, each embedded in a different crew:

  • Growth Infrastructure — focused on prospect acquisition: building a unified lead engine that captures, scores, routes, and nurtures across all channels

  • Product Platform — focused on member lifecycle messaging: operating Alan's messaging stack as a scalable service across 1.7M+ profiles

Both roles share the same DNA: strong marketing ops fundamentals, data fluency, a product mindset, and the ability to be both hands-on and strategic. Crew placement will be determined based on the candidate's experience, interests, and fit during the hiring process.

Why is this role interesting?

  • Speed: marketing, product, and sales teams ship campaigns and messages confidently — Marketing Ops turns bottlenecks into force multipliers across every crew

  • Trust: clean data, governed attributes, proper segmentation, and enforced rules mean the right person gets the right message at the right time

  • Scale: as we grow to millions of members across multiple countries, we need operators who keep our platforms clean and the user experience protected — without scaling headcount linearly

  • AI at the frontier: this isn't a maintenance role — you'll identify high-priority use cases for AI agents, train and refine them to a senior marketer's quality bar, and drive real adoption

What will you do with us?

You'll be a partnership with marketers — not a service desk. You'll partner closely with engineers, data, designers, and cross-functional stakeholders (PMMs, sales, growth, product) within a PM-Tech duo crew model.

Regardless of crew, you will own a core set of capabilities:

  • Marketing Automation & CRM: own and optimize our marketing stack (Customer.io, CRM integrations); build automations that enable marketers to launch campaigns independently, at scale, across all geos

  • Data Model & Governance: maintain CRM data quality, attribute/event design, and database hygiene as a sustained practice

  • Segmentation & Lifecycle Design: design and maintain lifecycle stages, segmentation logic, routing rules, and re-engagement flows across multiple audiences and geos

  • Nurturing Infrastructure: own the nurturing stack and campaign processes; make launches autonomous and compliant

  • AI-First Operations: identify, build, and refine AI agents for email copywriting, lead scoring, next-best-action recommendations, and content generation — making marketers AI-powered, not replacing them

  • Performance Monitoring: track the full funnel from first touchpoint to conversion; identify leakage and prioritize from data

  • Documentation & Enablement: create playbooks, train teams on tools and processes, reduce the marginal cost of new campaigns

Then, depending on your crew:

Growth Infrastructure — you'll build a unified lead engine (no more tool-by-tool silos), design lead scoring and routing models, crack multi-channel activation (email, WhatsApp, Voice AI), build AI agents that pre-qualify and enrich leads, and maintain a live feedback loop with BDRs, AEs, and Inbound Sales.

Product Platform — you'll operate Customer.io and back-end triggered emails as one governed system, monitor communication pressure and enforce channel rules, define and enforce recipient lifecycle paths, drive 100% Design Studio adoption, and co-own outbound messaging strategy with PMMs and product teams.

By your first year, we'll know it worked when:

  • At least one AI agent is in production on a key use case (email nurturing, lead categorization, content generation), with a second scoped or live, and adoption is real

  • Any marketer or product Alaner can launch a campaign or ship a message without bottlenecking through ops or engineering

  • CRM data model, attributes, and segments are properly owned, documented, and clean — the data we see is data we can act on

  • Every contact has a documented path through our messaging — segmentation is sharp, messaging is relevant, and pressure is monitored

  • Marketing's contribution to acquisition and engagement is visible and quantifiable, from first touch to conversion


⭐️ Is it you we are looking for? ⭐️


You'll be a great fit for this opportunity if you:

  • Have 5+ years in Marketing operations, growth ops, CRM ops, lifecycle marketing, or lead generation in a tech environment (B2B, B2C, or B2B2C)

  • Have hands-on experience managing marketing automation platforms at scale (Customer.io, Braze, Iterable, HubSpot, Marketo, Pardot, Salesforce, or equivalent)

  • Have a strong understanding of CRM data models — attribute/event design and data hygiene as a sustained practice

  • Can frame and implement processes for lead scoring, nurturing, segmentation, and personalization

  • Have a product knack: you can define what's not working, identify what to build next, and see problems as opportunities to bring more value

  • Bring data fluency and analytical rigor: you read platform and campaign data, surface anomalies, and draw business insights

  • Can be both hands-on and think strategically — you drive the big picture while staying close to execution

  • Have strong stakeholder management skills — you'll partner daily with engineering, product, sales, and marketing teams

  • Can manage multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-moving environment

  • Communicate with excellent written and spoken English

  • Are impact-driven with a strong bias towards improving processes

For this opportunity, we are aiming to hire within the C0-D level range.

🙌 Perks & Benefits

At Alan, we believe that being in good health is a basic need, and it starts with our employees. This is why Alaners are provided with a stimulating environment and perks ensuring they are happy, efficient and spend only high-quality time with co-workers.

Prévenir est un nouveau Service de Prévention et de Santé au Travail Interentreprises (SPSTI) en Île-de-France.

Notre ambition est de repenser la santé au travail pour améliorer l'impact sur la vie des salariés et l'expérience des professionnels de santé, en s'appuyant sur les moyens technologiques d'Alan.

Notre premier centre médical a ouvert ses portes au 117 Quai de Valmy (Paris 10ᵉ) et ce n'est que le début !

Vous êtes Assistant(e) Social(e) au sein d'une équipe pluridisciplinaire (médecins du travail, ASST, IPRP) avec laquelle vous co-construisez la pratique de Prévenir. Votre temps se répartit entre :

  • Accompagnement des salarié(es) dans leurs démarches sociales : retour d'arrêt, difficultés budgétaires, aidants, addictions, orientation vers les dispositifs

  • Une équipe pluridisciplinaire à co-construire. Vous ne rejoignez pas un service figé : vous participez à dessiner la place du Psychologue du Travail chez Prévenir, les protocoles de délégation avec les médecins, et les passerelles avec Assistant Sociaux et IPRP

  • Des outils numériques co-construits avec vous. Une équipe d'ingénieurs et de designers Alan développe avec les soignants les outils dont ils ont besoin, DMST, parcours de prévention, supports de webinaires, expérimentations IA

  • Le mix présentiel / distanciel pensé comme un atout métier. Vous voyez les salariés et les entreprises sur le terrain quand c'est utile, et vous gardez le temps et les outils pour faire de la prévention de qualité à distance le reste du temps

  • Écoute, sang-froid, indépendance et sens de l'équipe pluridisciplinaire

  • Basé·e en Île-de-France ; à l'aise avec un fonctionnement hybride et les outils numériques

  • Lieu : 117 quai de Valmy (Paris 10ᵉ) - dans un centre tout neuf, pensé pour la qualité de l'exercice médical

Health can’t wait.

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prévenir est un nouveau Service de Prévention et de Santé au Travail Interentreprises (SPSTI) en Île-de-France.

jobs.title: Lead Solution Architect – D365 F&O Finance & SCM (f/m/x)
jobs.description:
Our goal is to have a solar system on every roof, a storage unit in every house, and an electric car in every garage. Enpal makes this possible with an integrated total solution for decentralized energy—from solar systems and battery storage to wall boxes, smart meters, and heat pumps. At the heart of it all is our AI-powered platform Enpal.One+, which intelligently connects thousands of systems and efficiently optimizes electricity procurement and feed-in on the energy market.

Are you ready for solutions that are more than just a promise and bring real quality of life to thousands of households every day? What you create at Enpal will deliver clean electricity tomorrow and bring about lasting change in how we use energy.

What you'll do

Enpal is transforming its ERP landscape from a traditional D365 F&O setup into an Agentic Enterprise, a clean D365 core with an AI-native execution layer on top. AI-native product squads, organized by E2E process domain (D2O, O2C, P2P, SCE, R2R, MDG), replace traditional workstream towers. Each squad includes a Business Intent Owner (BIO), a Technology Orchestrator, Context Engineers, and Harness Engineers. This role sits in the Finance (R2R, O2C, MDG) squad and is a core contributor to building the agentic operating model that will power Enpal at scale.

As A Lead Solution Architect, you own the Finance & SCM architecture across D365 F&O, defining how GL, AP, AR, Fixed Assets, Cash & Bank, and Project Accounting are structured, governed, and evolved across 30+ legal entities. You set the design standards that functional consultants, developers, and partners work within, lead the decisions that are hard to reverse, and ensure that the Finance platform is the trusted, auditable system of record that a complex, multi-entity enterprise demands. In the agentic enterprise, you are also the architectural authority for the Finance agent layer, ensuring that Continuous Close Agents, Revenue Assurance Agents, and Collections Agents operate on a platform that is deterministic, traceable, and financially compliant.

FINANCE ARCHITECTURE & AGENTIC FOUNDATION

  • Define, govern, and evolve the Finance architecture across modules: GL, AP, AR, Fixed Assets, Cash & Bank, Project Accounting, and Cost Accounting

  • Design the architectural foundation for Finance AI agents, ensuring the D365 core provides the deterministic ledger, traceable decisions, and full audit trail that agentic operations require

  • Ensure alignment with enterprise architecture, regulatory requirements (IFRS/local GAAP), and global design principles across all legal entities

  • Translate complex Finance business requirements into robust D365 F&O designs, clean-core first, with customizations only where legally required or business-critical

STANDARDIZATION & GLOBAL ROLLOUT

  • Drive standardization, harmonization, and process simplification across regions and legal entities, ensuring the pilot BU design is locked and rolled out consistently

  • Ensure all Finance solutions are designed in a reliable, robust, and scalable way, ready for rollout across 30+ legal entities in the M9–M15 timeframe

  • Lead solution governance, blueprinting, and architectural decision-making across the Finance domain

  • Provide thought leadership on best practices, industry trends, and Microsoft ecosystem capabilities, including Copilot Studio, Azure AI Foundry, and Microsoft Fabric

DELIVERY LEADERSHIP & STAKEHOLDER MANAGEMENT

  • Provide hands-on guidance to functional consultants, developers, and integration teams, ensuring high-quality delivery across design, build, testing, cutover, and hypercare

  • Ensure high-quality delivery across design, build, testing, cutover, and support phases

  • Represent Finance architecture in ERP governance forums, design authority reviews, and steering committees up to CFO level

What you'll bring

  • Extensive experience in ERP Finance & SCM transformation, with significant hands-on experience in D365 F&O Finance across multiple modules and global rollouts

  • Proven architectural leadership designing end-to-end Finance solutions, including integrations, data models, extensions, and ISV evaluations, ideally within high-growth or complex organizations

  • Deep functional expertise in core Finance processes (GL, AP, AR, FA, Cash & Bank, Project Accounting, Cost Accounting) and strong understanding of IFRS/local GAAP

  • Strong fluency in D365 F&O architecture, including data entities and integration patterns

  • Understanding of or strong interest in agentic AI in Finance: how Continuous Close Agents, Revenue Assurance Agents, and Collections Agents operate, and what the platform must provide to support them

  • Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders, including Finance Directors and CFO, with clear communication and decision-making

  • Experience leading global implementations across multiple legal entities, including fit-gap analysis, blueprinting, solution governance, and change management

  • Collaborative leadership mindset that brings cross-functional teams together and drives clarity in complex global programs

  • Fluency in English; German is a plus

Are you interested even if you don't meet all the requirements? Apply anyway! We look forward to discovering your potential—regardless of whether your experience meets every single requirement. ☀️

Why this role matters

Finance is the most governance-critical domain in Enpal's ERP transformation. In the agentic enterprise, Finance agents, Continuous Close, Revenue Assurance, Collections & Credit, will automate the workflows that today consume weeks of manual effort across 30+ legal entities. As Lead Functional Consultant – D365 F&O Finance & SCM, you design the platform those agents operate on. The quality of your architecture directly determines the auditability, accuracy, and scalability of Enpal's financial operations at scale.

What we offer

With Workflex, we offer you the opportunity to relocate abroad for up to 30 days a year, depending on your responsibilities.

  • Grown-up business & startup spirit - In our modern office in Berlin-Friedrichshain, you'll find everything your heart desires, from height-adjustable desks and table tennis to stocked beverage fridges and barista coffee.

jobs.title: Director of People Operations
jobs.description:
About Us

Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar.

Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes.

2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler.

We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law.

Joining Legora means three things.

  • We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.

  • We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.

  • We grow together: as a team and with our customers.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.


The role
This role owns how it works to be an employee at Legora on the backend. You will operationalise every stage of the employee journey, making sure every moment is supported by clean systems, accurate data, and processes that scale. If an employee interacts with a Legora program or system, from their first day in the HRIS to a salary change three years in, your team is accountable for making it accurate, timely, and smooth.

You will lead a distributed People Operations team across Stockholm and New York, reporting to the VP, People Operations. As we enter new markets, you will also build and manage local specialisms to handle day-to-day employee and manager questions and run structured, lower-complexity casework, with a clean handoff to Employee Relations for anything that becomes formal, contested, or carries legal weight.



What you'll own

  • The full employee lifecycle, operationally. Every touchpoint from offer to exit, mapped, documented, and supported end to end.

  • HRIS and data integrity. Onboarding new hires into the HRIS, data entry, and data QA. You keep employee data accurate, complete, and audit-ready as the single source of truth.

  • Contracts and changes. Addendums, employee transfers, salary and reporting-line changes, and the workflows and documentation behind each one, working in close partnership with Payroll so every change flows through accurately and on time.

  • Benefits and leave administration. Run the day-to-day administration of benefits and leave across our markets. Total Rewards owns the policies, plan design, and philosophy; your team makes sure they are executed cleanly for every employee. Anything contested, discriminatory, or medically complex is escalated to Employee Relations.

  • Local HR Generalist build-out. As Legora enters new markets, hire, ramp, and manage the local HR Generalist / People Advisor-Ops layer: the in-market presence for day-to-day employee and manager questions, and for structured, lower-complexity casework such as absence management, recurring capability concerns, and restructuring conversations. These roles report into People Operations for management and delivery, with a dotted line to the regional Employee Relations Director for sign-off on jurisdictional readiness and casework quality.

  • Systems and tooling. Run the People tech stack (HiBob, Ashby, Ironclad), drive adoption, and take manual work out of the process.

  • Process and SOPs. Design scalable, well-documented processes for every program employees touch, and keep reducing friction and cycle time.

  • Compliance and controls. Partner with Legal and Finance to keep operations compliant across our markets, including working time, leave, and entity or EOR transitions, with a clean escalation path to Employee Relations for anything that becomes formal or carries legal weight.

  • Reporting. Own people data quality and the reporting backbone that powers People analytics for the business.



What you'll bring

  • 8+ years in People Operations or HR Operations, including leading a team and building out local, in-market HR capability as a company scales into new geographies, ideally in a high-growth or global company.

  • Deep HRIS expertise across complex, multidisciplinary system landscapes, with a strong interest in data quality, integrations, AI and tools.

Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. • 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking, tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

Relay delivers 400,000 parcels a day through people who don't work for us: van drivers who choose their own shifts, local shops that hold parcels, and couriers who take them to the door. We went from 3,000 parcels a day in London to 400,000 across the UK in under three years.

Parcel delivery has a quality problem the industry has learned to live with. Parcels go missing between depots. Parcels get marked as delivered and never reach the customer. Most carriers treat a steady rate of loss as a cost of doing business. Relay is building the delivery company where that stops being true.

That is harder for us than for most, because nearly everyone who touches a Relay parcel is an independent partner. We can't manage them into performance. We have to build the standards, the evidence and the product that make doing the job well the natural outcome. Engineering builds the product changes you design.

Partner Excellence Highlights

  • You own decision-making, not the model: you decide which signals count, which checks become rules, and whether each fix belongs in product, policy or training. The squad lead acts on your calls.

  • Most of a parcel's journey happens between scans. How do you prove a handover happened without making the job slower for the people doing it?

  • A delivery is marked complete and the customer says it never came. How do you tell a wrong address from a handover that went wrong, and put the fix where it belongs: product, policy or training?

  • Some checks can only answer "can't tell". Which are worth making provable, and which should we stop measuring?

  • A whole area, not a slice: you decide what evidence a whole network runs on, and the result is on the street the next morning.

  • Analytics at the front, not in support: the squad's roadmap follows the analysis, in a data team of about 30 across analytics, operational research and data science.

The Opportunity

As a Senior Decision Scientist, Partner Excellence at Relay, you'll:

  • Decide which Partner Excellence problems are real and which only look real, before anyone builds a fix.

  • Design how Partner Excellence decides: which signals count, what evidence the network runs on, and what good looks like.

  • Tell the squad lead what to change and what to stop, and get a decision.

  • Build the thing that decides: data applications, monitors and alerts, not decks, using Claude and agents to ship your own tools.

  • Go and look when the data and the street disagree: the sort centre, the van, the shop.

  • Get the missing data built, and prove which fixes worked. In a year, the squad can prove every handover in the network.

We're looking for candidates who…

  • Have owned fraud, risk or trust decisions end to end: turned investigations into rules, standards or interventions, and owned their number, such as the false positive rate you were held to, rather than building the model.

  • Have run investigations in fraud, risk, financial crime or trust and safety, and decided whether a signal was real or noise.

  • Have seen their work acted on: a leader changed a plan, a team adopted your method, or engineers built what you asked for.

  • Have worked somewhere with enough volume for a false positive rate to mean something, where your rules ran live and something happened when they were wrong.

  • Have got records created by teams who didn't report to you, and know how long it takes.

  • Are hands-on and fluent in SQL, with or without AI, and would rather ship a working answer this week than a perfect one next quarter. No logistics experience needed, just the appetite to learn a physical operation fast.

Don't tick every box? If this problem excites you, we'd still love to hear from you.

  • Play to Win: You chase bold bets, tackle the hard stuff, and view constraints as fuel, not friction.

  • 1% Better Every Day: You believe that small, consistent improvements lead to exponential growth. You move quickly, deliver results, and learn from every experience.

  • All In, All the Time: You show up and step up. You take ownership from start to finish and do what it takes to deliver when it counts.
